July: Friday the 6th, we are not sitting; we have some time off the week after that, that was announced already on a specific request of Mr. Emmerson; Friday the 13th, I think we still have to look at how that will be in view of the whole of that week; but we also intend not to sit on the 20th of July -- am I now mixing up -- let me just check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Friday, the 20th of July, we'll not be sitting, but for July the same is valid that if there would be any specific need we might decide otherwise, in view of the circumstances at that moment, and that might, especially on Friday, the 20th of July, which is one of the last, last days before our break and the recess. Good afternoon. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gashi, before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The usher will hand out to you, now, the text of this solemn declaration. May I ask you to stand and to make that solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gashi. You'll first be examined by Mr. Re, who's counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Is your name Medin Gashi?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were you born on the 3rd of February, 1980?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were born in Peje, in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is your father the late Kemajl Gashi?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Kemajl, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What year was your father born?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In 1998, where was your father living?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: In Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was he living with?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: With his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you living with him?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: We lived separately. He lived in one room; I lived in another room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he 43 in that year?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I think so, yes. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 65 ter Exhibit 760?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: My father worked at a shoe factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Making shoes?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he a member of any political organisation?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please? I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he a Kosovo Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: He was an Albanian of Kosovo, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was his religion?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number for the ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P325, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you look at the photograph on the screen in front of you? Is that a photograph of your late father, Kemajl Gashi?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was your father -- were you aware of your father's political affiliations in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of whether he had sympathies for the Serbian authorities in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was working for or with the Serbian authorities in Kosovo in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: To my recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "to my recollection"?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because I was very young at that time, and I don't remember whether he did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were you working at in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You.

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I -- I tried to -- to do everything. I sold produce and -- at the bazaar, doing -- working as a mechanic, any work I could find.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In the middle of 1998, were you living in Peje?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of the existence of the UCK or KLA in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question because I didn't understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You know what the KLA is?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know about them in the middle of 1998, when you were working and living in Peje?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you know about them?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: That it is an army, our army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "our army"?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: An army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For the Kosovar Albanians, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you sympathise with the aims of the KLA against the Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Can you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you believe in what they were doing in fighting the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because I wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you want to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: This is how I thought, how I felt, together with my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was it about the KLA that made you want to join it?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness be asked to repeat his answer? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gashi, could you please repeat your last answer because the interpreters could not hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because I liked to join it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you want to join it? Can you tell the Trial Chamber -- no one here knows you. We want to know why you wanted to join the KLA in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I liked it. I wished to join.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, if I may just intervene for one second. From reading the statement of the witness, it gave the impression that what the witness knew about the KLA, what actually moved him to join, et cetera, seems not to be the core of the testimony we would expect. Of course, if there's any specific relevance to explore this field in quite some detail, then of course I'm not going to stop you. But it gave me the impression that the events that happened after he had joined were of major importance for the testimony rather than exactly the motivations and knowledge, and so this is -- I asked -- I urge the parties to see whether they could move as efficiently as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you come to join the KLA? What did you do to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I went there with a woman from Klicine. There we joined -- I joined the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've been told I can't lead, otherwise I would have led him on where he went to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm happy for Mr. Re to lead on essential matters of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As soon as I'm not happy for him to lead, I'll indicate, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you go to -- did you join the KLA in Barane?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you go there through Klicine village and arrive in Brelic on the way, and there was a KLA check-point in Brelic?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you got to Barane, did you report to the KLA headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That point has now been reached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you go to Barane? What other KLA --

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Went there to join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why Barane? Were there other KLA places you could have gone to?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because it was closer to where I lived, and I didn't know any other place other than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened when you got to -- sorry, I withdraw that. Whereabouts in Barane was the KLA headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: At a school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph which is 65 ter 1343, and while that's coming I'll ask you another question. Who did you speak to when you got to the school?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Me -- I entered the headquarters, I reported there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did you report to and what was their response when you reported there?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: The guard took me into the office where I reported. Initially, they did not want -- didn't want to take me on because I was too young. I begged them that I wanted to join, and they finally did relent and accept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just look at the photograph on the screen there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P326, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that the school in Barane where you went?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember going to an oath-taking ceremony in Barane in the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long after you joined the KLA in Barane was that oath-taking ceremony, just approximately, days or weeks?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Probably a week or two, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If I tell you that the date marked on the video is the 20th of July, 1998, does that help your memory?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you joined the KLA, were you given training or weapons or uniform?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, no uniform. A weapon I got two weeks later. We were trained.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of training did you do and where did you do it?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: In the -- in the fields around, we got trained there. We ran, as usual, different exercises.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just very briefly tell -- tell the Court what those usual different exercises were?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: We ran, we played football, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about military training, did you receive any military-type training?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, but not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you do any military-type exercises?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, very little, three, four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was training you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: There was a military man called Ardijan from Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he in uniform?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you do any military training such as digging trenches or martial arts, or any of the other normal types of military training?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember how long you stayed in the KLA in terms of days, weeks, or months?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No. It seems like three and a half weeks or four, but I can't exactly remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of weapon were you given after about two weeks?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Popov 10-millimetre.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of weapon is that: Long-arm or short-arm?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: It's a rifle, the brand name is Popov, 10-millimetre.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there other recruits taking part in this training and these exercises you did?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did you do the training with?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: With friends. The training was conducted by Ardijan from Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you staying?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I didn't understand this. Can you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you staying in the school?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, at the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you sleeping?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: On the second floor of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many other people were sleeping there?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know. There were many, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "many," do you mean more than ten, less than ten, more than 20, less than 20, 50, 100? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Where we were, probably in one and the same room there were 20, 22 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many KLA soldiers were in the school, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about duties, what duties were you given after you were given your rifle?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Cleaning, guarding duties in the kitchen, helping out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were your guard duties? What were you guarding?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I was a guard with a weapon, with a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you guarding the school?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is Musa Draga?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: My commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know him before you joined the KLA in Barane?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you go to the oath-taking ceremony in Barane?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just going to play you a short clip of video Exhibit D41 from timer --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before that's played, may I just raise one matter, perhaps with the witness's earphones not on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gashi, do you understand any English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take off your earphones for a second, please? Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour will recall this videotape has a Defence exhibit number because it was a document that was to be used in the cross-examination of Rrustem Tetaj, but which was not, in fact, used because of time constraints --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You announced that it would be played today --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In cross-examination. But Mr. Re is obviously going to play it in chief. In order to avoid duplication and to save time, the video will show Tahir Zemaj and Ramush Haradinaj both standing together on the platform addressing this group of recruits, and rather than take time asking the witness to go through and identify the individuals concerned, if I can simply draw Your Honour's attention to that fact. There is also an individual who is walking up and down the line examining the troops, it might be helpful for this witness to identify that individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, no, it's not acceptable. Mr. Emmerson is just taking a chunk of my time. I wish to show the witness one minute of the video just to identify the video. That's it. I'm not following his suggestions as to who I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then we'll have to play it later on, again. I'll allow --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's up to him how he conducts his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Mr. Emmerson, in deviation from the normal order is allowed, once you've played that, to ask the witness to identify a person he's interested in which avoids us to play it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does many Emmerson have the timer? I mean, he told me before -- I could have taken him to this. I have a selection from 3 minutes 26 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sorry, let's proceed--

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't know where he wants to go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, let's proceed. Show the video to the witness. And I do understand that identification of the other persons is not needed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just showing the witness for the record at timer 3.26 to 4.38 of Exhibit D41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I didn't see anyone walking in the background, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In fact, from that passage the question can be asked, and it's -- because the individual concerned, although not walking up and down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I'll allow you to do that after Mr. Re has put his questions in relation to this. And if you would have the exact time moment, then we could already ask that portion to be -- to be retrieved for your question. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Gashi, did you see that video, I think, for the first time yesterday in the offices of the Prosecution, here?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did you view the whole video which goes for about an hour and a half?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you attend that ceremony?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I didn't see myself there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember where you were in the ceremony?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know because it was a bit crowded. There was many people there and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You weren't one of the soldiers wearing a uniform standing as people were speaking to them?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I was without a uniform --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Was that then made clear by the witness that this was the very ceremony he himself also attended?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to clarify that for Judge -- for the Judges, you were there but you couldn't see yourself in video?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And do you remember Ramush Haradinaj addressing the soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know him before that or had you ever heard of him or seen him before that day?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No. Only on television I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before or after?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, no, before, when I was in Peje, before going to -- before going to Barane. I heard people talking about Ramush, Ramush, but I hadn't seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did you connect the Ramush, Ramush, with the person who was addressing the soldiers when you saw -- when you were there that day? I mean, was that the same Ramush, is what I'm asking you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what about Tahir Zemaj, do you remember him being there talking to the crowd?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Those are my questions on the video, if Mr. Emmerson wants to interpose now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There's one issue which is not entirely clear. You said you had seen Mr. Haradinaj on television. Mr. Re asked you whether that was before or after the ceremony. You said before and you heard people talking about Ramush, Ramush. Did you already before the ceremony see him on television or did you just hear about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had heard about him, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not seen him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you also at that time had seen him on television already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, if there's any specific portion, would you please point at it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's simply one question, and it may be that it can be dealt with without the witness viewing the video again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At the very end of that passage of video, there was a man standing on the platform addressing the group of soldiers. Can I ask you this: Do you know who Nazif Ramabaja is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you know the identity of the man who is shown in that -- in that very last piece of footage that we saw standing on the balcony addressing the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you take the oath with the other soldiers in that oath-taking ceremony shown in the video?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you given a certificate of membership after taking the oath?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you still have that or what happened to it?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Once you joined the KLA in Barane, did you go home to visit your family while you were still in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about your sister, you've got a sister called Ganimete?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes. She was in Buqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How far is Buqan from Barane?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: About 90 minutes, one hour, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that by foot?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see her while you were staying in the school of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there someone there called Agim at the school of the KLA with you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: A colleague of mine. I shared a room with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was he from? What was his village?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: He was from Rasuje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How far is Rasuje from Barane?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Probably one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, did he ask you to do something one day?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: To me, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he tell you, you had to go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, to an office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he say to you about what you had to do?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: He came up to the room, and he said I should go downstairs because Musa Draga was asking for me. I went downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: To the office of Musa Draga.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was his office?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: It was on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of the school?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did Musa Draga say to you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Musa Draga told me to go to Mete.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, who's Mete?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Mete Krasniqi. Before he was known as Mete Vranoci.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: He was a military police officer. He was wearing a black uniform. I don't know what his rank was or his duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Musa Draga told you to go and meet -- go to Mete. Did you go to Mete?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: To Mete's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was Mete office?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Mete's office was about 100 metres from the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you can't see that in the photograph of the school I showed you before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you go with anyone else to Mete's office or did you go by yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: On my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, is Mete still alive?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened to Mete?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you know that he's dead then?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: That's what people are saying, that he's dead, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of building was Mete's office in? Can you describe the building to the Trial Chamber, what it was made of and how many rooms it had?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, there were two rooms. I saw a corridor and a room. It was 100 metres away from the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many floors or storeys did the building have?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: It was a one-floor building.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you go inside the building?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was in there?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Mete and two others.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said a moment ago, Mete was wearing a black uniform. What about the other two?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, they were wearing a black uniform; or yes, they were wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I didn't quite focus my attention on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether they were uniformed?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, no. I think they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they armed, that's any of the three?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Arms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whereabouts was Mete when you went into the building? You described a corridor and a room. Where was Mete?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: In the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it a corridor that came directly from the door as you came in or was it somewhere else? I mean, did you walk directly into a corridor?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did Mete say to you -- just stop for a moment. I'm sorry. Was there any furniture in that corridor that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did Mete say to you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: As soon as I entered, he told me, You are the son of the spy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did he say that to you, in what -- in what tone of voice?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Not very loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your response when he said, You are the son of a spy?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I said, That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What else did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ask him anything about the allegation or the statement that you were the son of a spy?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Nothing happened. I asked to leave, and I was told that, Your father has been taken to here with a police jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who said that?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Mete said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were the people with him?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned going to Musa Draga's office before. Do you remember whether Musa Draga --

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- was there?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said Mete said: "Your father has been taken to here with a police jeep." What did you understand him to mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I understood that he had been taken as a spy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because this is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of police jeep did you understand Mete to be referring to?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: A Serb police jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you understand him to be referring to a Serb police jeep?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because we didn't have our own police at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was your father when you were having this conversation with Mete and the two others were there?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: In the room, in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which room are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: In Mete's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described a corridor. Where was this room in relation to where you were standing -- where you were and where Mete was?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: There was one room and one corridor. The corridor was like an entrance to Mete's office, which was the first room on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On the left as you came in through the door or as you were going out?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: The room was on the left side, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As you were entering the building or as you were leaving the building?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which one? As you came in, was it on the left; or if you were going out, was it on the left?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: As you went in the corridor, it was on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did that door -- did that room have a door on it?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it open or closed?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: It was closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you know your father was in that room?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because I heard his screams.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Describe to the Trial Chamber what you heard.

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: He was only screaming.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How loudly?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Not very loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know it was your father?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because I -- when I entered, Mete told me that, You are the spy's son, so this is how I thought that it was my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you recognise the screams as his?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: From the noise you heard coming from that room, was there anything to indicate whether or not there were any other people in that room with your father? What I'm saying to you: Did it sound like he was alone in there or were there other people there?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I thought he was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What gave you the impression that he was alone?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because I heard only one voice, from the voice I could surmise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear any other noises coming from that room, apart from the screaming you've just described?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I didn't get an answer then.

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you just say yes or no to the answer -- to the question I asked you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did that go on for, the screaming?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: As long as I remained there. After I left, I don't know whether he continued screaming.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately how long were you in that corridor for?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Not for very long, seven or eight minutes, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you come to leave the corridor?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I didn't leave. They came and fetched me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is they?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Musa Draga and Ibra.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Ibra, did you say?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Ibra.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is Ibra? What's his family --

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: A colleague of mine who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did Musa Draga and Ibra do when they came to fetch you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Just, they took me away and we went to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did they take you away? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: They told Mete that, We have come to take this guy. Mete said to them that, He's the spy's son. And then I said, This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they touch you at all?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, just took me by the hand and we went together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you said that, you just touched your right arm with your left hand. Can you just show us that again?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, they touched me by the arm and then we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you mean "touched you by the arm"? Did they take you by the arm or just touch you on the arm?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: They took me by the arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you mean physically?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No. We just went together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that the three of you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go to or where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: To my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying back to the accommodation you had in the school?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before then and hearing your father screaming, when was the last time you had seen your father before then?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I didn't see my father at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you joined the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes. He was in Peje when I went to join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When -- before you joined the KLA, when was the last time -- how long before you joined the KLA was the last time you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Three weeks or three weeks and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, after you heard him screaming in the room and you said you were taken back to your -- with Mete and you were taken back to your room in the school, did you see your father again after hearing him scream in that room?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: On the next day, when I went out in the yard and lit a cigarette, I saw him for two or three seconds coming out of Mete's office and entering.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And entering -- sorry? You saw him coming out --

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I saw him going back to Mete's room, office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: He was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how far away from you -- how far were you from him when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: 100 or 120 metres, not farther than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you recognise it was your father?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I recognised it by his shirt and by the training suit he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there anything else about him that enabled you to recognise him, apart from his clothes?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No. He had that training suit, a shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ever see your father again after those few seconds, the day after you'd heard him screaming in the room next to Mete office?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did any other members of your family tell you about seeing him after that?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- who was it and what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: My sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right, that's Ganimete?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did she tell you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: My sister was in Buqan, and I don't know where she saw him or where she met my father, but he told her, I am leaving. These are the words she told me he had said to her. I don't know more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did she say she had seen him?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know, but my sister was in Buqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: By when -- by what I mean "see him," I mean was it in the street, in a house, in a police station, by --

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: In the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did your sister tell you this?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: After the war, when I was in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What year was that?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: 2001, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember -- did your sister say when it was she'd seen your father?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No. She didn't mention the date. She simply said that she had seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you come to leave the KLA in Barane?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: What? Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You told us a little while ago that you were in the KLA, I think -- I think you said for three and a half weeks?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you leave the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because everybody left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Everybody left where?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know. Everybody went to his respective home.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Because they said that the Serbs are coming, so go, leave, and we left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I'm looking at the clock. Could you give an indication as where we are at this moment in time?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Possibly five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could try to reduce that to three minutes, then we stay within your time-limits that you gave yourself. Please proceed. But before doing so, I have one matter I'd like to clarify. Mr. Gashi, you said your sister told you that she had seen your father in Buqan. She told her -- this to you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a couple of years later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How -- what makes you so sure about your sister having seen your father after you had seen him in the barracks, in the office of Mete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I saw him there, but my sister saw him in Buqan, in the street, but I don't know where exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the question is: How do you know whether your sister had seen him before or after you had seen him in Mete's office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand your question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your sister tells you, I've seen our father in the village of Buqan. She tells this for years later when you're in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You personally observed your father walking into Mete's office and you heard his screams. Now, how do you know for sure that what your sister told you was after your father -- after you had seen your father in the barracks, in the office? Is there any possibility that your sister would have seen him prior to that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, she didn't see him before me. I was the first who saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, my question is: How do you know that for certain? What did your sister tell you that makes you -- yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because we talked together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And your sister was not aware or was she that your father had been seen by you in the office? Is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She knew because I told her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But when did you tell her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told my sister, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I met her in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But how was your sister then so sure -- how could she know when she saw him, you had seen him already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I was just asking you about when you left the KLA, and you said: "Everyone -- everybody went back to his respective home. The Serbs were coming." Was there a Serbian offensive or an attack?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you know there was a Serbian attack then?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: The colleagues there told me -- everybody left. It was not only me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you not go back to the KLA after leaving when you heard there was an attack coming?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I went to Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you not go back to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why? Why not?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Why should I go back when Mete told me, You are the spy's son? Why should I go back?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When Mete told you, you were the spy's son, did he tell you where your father had been seen in a Serbian police jeep?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know Mete from before the war?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he do before the war?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: He had a coffee shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that in Peje?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when he was telling you that you were the son of a Serbian spy and the other two were with him, what were your feelings? How were you feeling when he was talking to you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I felt very bad, of course, because I went to join the KLA voluntarily and to have him tell me that I am the son of a Serbian spy, of course I feel very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you feeling any fear when he was speaking to you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Describe the fear you were feeling.

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I was afraid he would beat me or do something bad to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you take off your earphones for a second? We'll have a break. I'll ask Mr. Usher to escort you out of the courtroom and we'll have a break for 20 minutes, but I want to -- yes, if you escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I have one matter which I'd like to raise with you. One of your last questions to the witness, you asked: "When Mete told you, you were the spy's son, did he tell you where your father had been seen in a Serbian police jeep?" I made earlier an notation for myself on the testimony in relation to the Serbian police jeep, because there you put the following question: You said: "Mete said your father has been taken to here with a police jeep. What do you understand this to be?" And the answer was: "A. I understood that he had been taken as a spy. "Q. Why did you understand this? "A. Because this is what he told me. "Q. What sort of police jeep did you understand?" "A. A Serb police jeep." And then the witness continues to say that they had no jeeps. Now, I have difficulties in grabbing what now actually happened, taken to a place in a police jeep is not -- I understood that to be taken by those who kept him there, whereas in your -- but perhaps that's a wrong understanding. Of course, I'm not a native English speaker. And later you said when he was seen in a police jeep. It makes sense to me that if you see someone in a Serb police jeep, that this raises the suspicion that he might be collaborating with the Serbs, but the "taken to" bothers me. "Your father has been taken to here," or "was he, together with the Serb police, going there being delivered?" It's just unclear to me. If there's any way that I misunderstood the testimony or -- please explain to me, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It should be -- of course it should be clarified. I was just very mindful of the three minutes I was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It should be clarified, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then -- Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just raising again the question of timing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break of 20 minutes, and as I promised during the break, I'll look at whether there's any possibility of other courts perhaps need to use this courtroom. We'll explore that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't know whether or not those few more minutes may take care of the problem or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Because the issue may go beyond Mr. Emmerson's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could Mr. Emmerson give a more precise estimate at this moment of what he would need if he would put all the questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was aiming for 45 to 50 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can shave some time of that, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So we would end up at 35, 40 minutes perhaps. I'm an optimist.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's very optimistic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I seem to -- I seem to inevitably draw the short straw. I'll try to get done that which I can in that period of time, I'll try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not entirely clear your answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again, I don't want to waste time during the break. It really depends on what questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So it's -- Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No straw at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No straw at all. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As a general estimate, unless anybody disagrees, if what Your Honour is asking how long we ought to be thinking of asking for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, I'm aiming for asking for another half-hour after --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That was going to be my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it's possible or not has yet to be seen, but that's what I'm aiming at. We'll have a break until quarter past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm glad to announce that everyone is making great efforts to support us. It's now quarter past 1.00. We are allowed to go on until quarter past 2.00, but not one minute longer. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Guy-Smith's been kind enough to indicate that he thinks cross-examination will, in his case, be short or non-existent.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gashi, I'm going to ask you some questions now on behalf of Ramush Haradinaj, and I want to start, if I may, by just clarifying certain dates with you. You made a statement to the Prosecution in this case on the 4th of August, 2006, in which you were interviewed by an investigator called Shahzada Sultan. Do you remember that interview with the Prosecution investigator?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At paragraph 9 of that statement, you said that as far as you could remember, the date on which you joined the KLA at Barane was a week or more before the oath-taking ceremony. And in paragraph 11 of the same statement, you said that it was about one and a half weeks before the oath-taking ceremony. I think in your testimony you said a week or two before the oath-taking ceremony. Now, we've seen from the videotape that the oath-taking ceremony took place on the 20th of July. So does it follow from that, Mr. Gashi, that the date on which you went to the Barane HQ was sometime between the 6th and the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gashi, could you answer the question right once you've heard it. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In paragraph 18 of that same witness statement to the Prosecution, you said that the incident, in which your father was detained and you heard him screaming, took place a week or so after the oath-taking ceremony in Barane. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that takes us to something in the area of the 27th of July. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've described seeing your father the following day walking in the area outside the school building in Barane and walking -- walking towards, is it, or away from the office of Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Walking towards the office of Mete Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You said he was alone at the time. Is that correct? Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you sure it was your father that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As far as you could see, was he in any form of custody at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want, if I may, just to ask you, during the weeks that followed was your sister living in Buqan?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you visit her in Buqan?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you visit her to take some washing and wash some clothes?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, but I was there only once to have my clothes washed and to take a bath.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know that your sister Ganimete has made a witness statement for the Prosecution in this case in October and November of 2006? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I please call-up and mark for identification Defence 1D410052?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D91, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, the original of this statement is in French because it was taken in Switzerland. We do not have an Albanian translation; we do have an English translation. And so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the French original uploaded in the system?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The French original is uploaded in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Gashi, I'm therefore going to read to you some paragraphs from your sister's witness statement and ask you to comment on them. Your sister describes an incident in which she herself was interviewed about the allegation that your father was a spy. Did you know that your sister had been interviewed as well?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At paragraph 14 of her witness statement, she describes what took place after that interview. And having been told that your father had been detained as a spy and having been interviewed herself, she says at paragraph 14: "I must have stayed in Buqan for a week, perhaps more. My neighbour's son was also a KLA member, and he was in the same barracks as my brother. When my brother found out I was there, he came twice to see me to give me his laundry to wash. According to what my brother told me, my father was still in the barracks, working in the kitchen." And she goes on: "At any rate, he did not tell me more. I must say that in the house in Buqan, we never had a moment where just the two of us could speak in private." Now, do you remember telling your sister that your father was still in the barracks working in the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it possible that you did tell her that but you can no longer remember it?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So do I take it that it is possible, therefore, that you did tell her that?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Maybe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us, do you remember having seen your father in the barracks from time -- you do? -- from time to time washing kitchen utensils in the yard. Do you remember seeing that?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't see him doing what you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the witness statement that you made for the Prosecution in August 2006 - and I'm looking now at, bear with me just a moment, paragraph 20 - you said this, and I'm quoting: "After I saw my father for the last time entering Mete's office, my sister saw him twice in the street in the village of Buqan."

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "She saw him maybe after about two weeks." And then you explain something about how his appearance changed in between those two occasions. You say: "When I say him, he had a small beard; while when she saw him, he had a long beard."

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: This is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that how you became clear in your mind that she had seen him alive and well after he was in the barracks? Is that how you reached that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, she saw him in a good condition in the street. I saw him also well and alive in the barracks, but I didn't see him anymore after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But when you saw him in the barracks, did you see any injuries on him?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No. He was 120 metres away from me. How could I see if you [as interpreted] had any injuries on him or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In paragraph 20 of your Prosecution witness statement, you go on to say: "She told me that she tried to approach him, but he did not talk to her." Now, I think in your evidence a little earlier on, you told us that she told you that your father had said to her, I am leaving?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What did you understand that to mean, leaving where or leaving what?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: He told my sister that, I'm leaving. He said, I'm leaving, I'm going home. That is all she told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But did you understand him to be saying he was leaving the KLA barracks in Barane?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, but he was not alone. He was with four or five other people. This is what my sister told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So he was with four or five other people, and did he, according to your sister -- according to your sister --

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: This is what she told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And according to your sister, did he seem to be well and moving freely of his own accord?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't ask her about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. But you do agree that what she was conveying to you was that your father was saying that he was leaving the KLA barracks and going home. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your statement continues at paragraph 20, Mr. Gashi: "It means that Mete released my father after detaining him for some time." Was that your understanding of what your sister had told you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want to turn to your sister's witness statement again, and just to remind you this is the October/November 2006 witness statement. Describing that incident, I'm just going to read to you what she says.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraphs 15 to 17: "After a week I wanted to return to Barane to see my brother, despite my fear of the soldiers. While I was walking on the road in Buqan with my neighbour, I heard someone behind me call out my nickname, Ganu. I turned around and it was my father. There stood my father, alone, wearing a T-shirt, shorts, and sandals. He had a rather bushy beard and rather long hair. I did not see any particular marks on his face or arms. I asked him what he was doing there, and he told me that he had worked in the kitchen in the Barane barracks, that he had given a hundred Deutschemarks to a soldier to let him escape, and that he was on his way to Pec. I told him that I was on my way to see Medin in Barane. He did not answer me and took off quickly towards Pec." Now, pause there. Is that what she told you, in effect?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. She also says, paragraph 17, that at the time she saw your father, there were KLA soldiers in the area who told her to turn around because there were bombings. And she continues: "We returned to my neighbour's house, and that evening or night soldiers came through the streets shouting that we had to leave because the Serbs were coming." Now, pausing there for a moment, Mr. Gashi, you told us that you and others left the Barane barracks because there was a Serb offensive approaching the area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you said that was after three and a half weeks. Is that correct or have I misunderstood your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, three weeks and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Three and a half weeks after what, after you joined or after you last saw your father?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: After I joined after -- no, after I saw my father, after I saw my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you -- if we can just put it together for a moment. The oath-taking ceremony was on the 20th. You say you saw your father roughly a week later, and that it was two weeks after that that your sister saw him. So that would be roughly three weeks after the oath-taking ceremony?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, three weeks. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When your sister saw your father, was that at the same time as the Serbian offensive was sweeping through the area, Mr. Gashi?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: No, it was not at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Do you remember, Mr. Gashi, on the 13th of September, speaking to a British police officer and an Albanian investigator who were conducting investigations on behalf of the Defence for Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was what you said to those people the truth, Mr. Gashi? Did you tell them the truth?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: The truth, as far as I could recollect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They made it clear to you, didn't they, that you were under no obligation to speak to them if you didn't want to?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told them you were perfectly happy to speak to them and to make a statement to them, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told them that everything in the statement that you made to them was true, to the best of your knowledge and memory, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you signed the statement on every page?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Before you signed it, it was read out to you in Albanian, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I please call-up on the screen Defence document identification 1D410025?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want to tender that, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I've given you the wrong one, I do apologise. It's 1D410017.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D92, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would it be possible for the Prosecution to get a hard copy of this? It's extremely hard to follow eight pages on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's there, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We will have a hard copy made available over the next few minutes, hopefully, if there's an unmarked version available. Is there an unmarked version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's move on. I take it that if someone finds it, it will be immediately given to Mr. Re. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I can't see anything on the screen at the moment, so -- oh, I'm sorry. My screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just going to go through it with you, if I may, Mr. Gashi, and I'll read it to you in English. I'm not going to read every paragraph. In the first paragraph, you describe who you are and describe the circumstances in which you came to make this statement. In the second paragraph you say this: "I was interviewed by an investigator from the ICTY about a month ago. He left his card with me and his name was Shahzada Sultan. I met him" -- and then we need to go to the next page, please. "I met him as a result of my uncle Agim Gashi, who normally resides in Austria, contacting the ICTY and alleging that I was involved in killing my father Kemajl Gashi." And you then go on to explain how it was that you had a discussion with the investigator and agreed to meet with him in Pristina. You describe, at the bottom of paragraph 2, some issues about your family background and your relationship with your father. And then if we can just turn over, please, to page 3, you say: "In 1998," this is at the bottom of the page, "in 1998, I joined the KLA in Lugi i Berani. When I joined, I was interviewed in a normal way. Recruits were always interviewed in this way and asked why they wanted to join. This was routine and I was accepted for service with the KLA. I didn't wear a uniform which wasn't" -- and then, please, over the page -- "which wasn't unusual at that time, some people did and some didn't." You then go on to describe the weapons with which you were issued, and you say that the overall commander for the region that Barane was in was Tahir Zemaj. And you say: "I never saw or heard of Ramush Haradinaj being in our area, and at that time I did not know of him." In the following paragraph, you describe your sister and you describe your father and say that both of them joined the KLA; your father joining at Barane. You say that he came under suspicion of association with the Serb MUP, and you say that he was interviewed and so were you and so was your sister Ganimete by a KLA officer called Mete Vranoci and another officer that you knew by the nickname of Ibra. You then go on to describe Vranoci as a violent man who you knew did not have a spotless character -- a spotless reputation, sorry. You go on then in the remainder of that paragraph, if you could just go over the following page to page 4, to describe -- to describe -- sorry, page 5, I'm sorry -- to describe the incident that you've told us about. You make some comments about your sister being threatened by Vranoci, and then you pick up what happened after that. And this is in the second main paragraph. Can we focus in on that, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, still too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say this, Mr. Gashi: "My father was allowed to remain with the KLA but he was not issued with a weapon of any kind. There were two parts to the HQ. One was the military part to which I was attached and the other part was the KLA police part. My father worked in this part so that we did not meet or talk to each other. Because my father was allowed to remain in the KLA although not issued with a weapon, I thought that the KLA senior officers must not be certain that he was a Serb collaborator, although perhaps they still had some suspicions about him. I sometimes saw him working in the garden, washing equipment from the kitchen." And then if we can just turn over to page 6, please, the final passage I need to read to you is on the first -- no, I'm sorry, this is the last passage, but it's the first paragraph of this page, page 6. Thank you. You then say: "In the summer of 1998, there was a large Serb offensive in the area of Barane and everybody left. I left and went first to Rosujaj, where I left my rifle with a friend. I then made my way back to Peje. My sister Ganimete arrived back home in Peje the next day. The last time I saw my father Kemajl alive was about one week before the Serb offensive. This was in Buqan where he was marching with other KLA soldiers. I noticed he was wearing a black or dark blue short-sleeved T-shirt and dark coloured trousers. He said to me, 'I am going home.' At that time he had a beard which was of medium length. He had not had this when he joined the KLA. Because my father had now been allowed to leave the KLA HQ, I thought he was now more trusted by the senior officers. I have not seen my father since that day." Now, Mr. Gashi, those extracts I've just read from your statement which you signed represent your best recollection, do they, at the time when you were interviewed by the Defence investigators of the truth of the position?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just go to the bottom of the page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature there on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MEDIN GASHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally this --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we look back to page 2 and to the first main paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You -- at this passage, you are commenting on the statement you made to the Prosecution investigator after you had just been informed that your father's remains had been positively identified.
